To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the problem of range queries is NP-complete; 2) there exists an algorithm that solves range queries for the SUM operation in O(nlogn) time, where n is the number of cells in the data cube; 3) there exists an optimal O(n) algorithm for range queries on data cubes of depth 1, where the number of cells is equal to the product of the number of values of the numeric dimensions.

(1) for range queries on OLAP data cubes, the SUM operation can be computed in time O ( n + m + k ), where n, m and k are the number of selected cells, number of dimensions, and number of selected cells on a given dimension, respectively; and (2) for range queries, the MAX operation can be computed by using the SUM operation in time O ( k log n ), where k is the number of selected cubes on a given dimension.
the SUM range query can be solved by a single scan of the data cube and the MAX range query can be answered by a single scan and a single aggregation operation over a small number of cells.
